title: SSO/KMS Onboarding: Incident Scenarios, Clarifications, and Acceptance Checklist
creator: Sanjay Patel
description: This ticket captures clarifications to the PRD for private deployment onboarding focusing on SSO/SAML federation, RBAC mapping, audit logging retention and schema, and KMS/HSM key custody integration. It also documents realistic incident scenarios we must validate during customer onboarding and the sign-off checklist for Security, Product, and Solutions teams. The goal is to close ambiguites from the PRD and produce a deterministic acceptance checklist that operators and customers can run during onboarding.
decisions: Adopt SAML 2.0 SP-initiated flow as default with IdP-initiated as opt-in (reason: predictable session lifecycle for operators)

RBAC will be expressed as two layers: identity-level roles (SAML attributes -> Redwood roles) and resource-level entitlements managed via Firebolt policy engine (reason: separation of concerns and auditability)
KMS integration will support two modes: customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (preferred) and HSM-backed offline escrow for air-gapped installs (reason: regulatory coverage)
Audit logs must include token-level metadata (route, model, commit hash) and be emitted to customer-configurable sinks with a canonical schema v2.1
acceptance_criteria: SSO: SP-initiated login with two sample IdPs (Okta, Azure AD) completes end-to-end in <3s under test harness
SAML attributes mapping: admin, billing, developer roles are mappable by config; mapping persisted and testable via API
RBAC: role changes (add/remove) propagate to session policy within 60s and are audited with before/after snapshots
KMS: customer-provided key can be registered, used for envelope encryption of tenant metadata, and rotated without downtime in a staged rollout
HSM: offline rotation procedure documented and runbook verified in dry-run with operator sign-off
Audit logs: retention TTL and immutability flags configurable; logs exported to S3 and Splunk with canonical v2.1 schema and no dropped events in 24h load test
Security review: threat model updated and signed by Security team; open risks <= 3 and mitigation plans tracked
Automation: onboarding checklist steps are runnable via the onboarding CLI with pass/fail exit codes for each gating step
scope_changes: Scope narrowed: remove initial support for LDAP binding in the first private release (reason: low demand and complexity). LDAP deferred to follow-up epic PM-892000
Scope expanded: include explicit audit schema versioning and migration tooling (added after privacy/legal request)
Clarified: HSM mode will not be offered as managed HSM in hosted Cloud for this release; only customer-managed HSM in private air-gapped installs
test_scenarios: IdP failover: simulate primary IdP outage, ensure SP falls back to secondary IdP within 30s with no loss of active sessions beyond configured grace window
Role drift: change mapping on IdP side and verify Redwood reflects expected role changes in <60s and emits audit entries
Key rotation: perform key rotation with simulated active requests, assert no plaintext exposure and no request failures above 0.5%
Audit pipeline loss: drop 10% of audit events in ingestion for 2 minutes and verify dedupe/retry mechanisms recover events and SLA meets specified recovery time
Compromise scenario: simulate compromised operator credential and ensure KMS key usage audit shows no unauthorized unwrap operations and that emergency key-revocation runbook is executable
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal validation (security + SRE) — run full test harness against staging private cluster
Phase 2: Pilot with 3 enterprise customers under NDA — collect telemetry and incident scenarios
Phase 3: General availability for Private deployments after sign-off and one-week operational burn-in

risk_mitigation: Mitigation A: IdP outage — require secondary IdP configuration and documented failover test during onboarding
Mitigation B: Key compromise — require key-use attestation and emergency rotation runbook; minimize plaintext handling
Mitigation C: Audit loss — add local write-ahead buffer with X-ack guarantees before acknowledging requests
monitoring_alerts: Alert: SAML assertion error rate > 1% sustained for 5m
Alert: Audit sink backlog > 10k events or oldest event age > 12h
